Title: ?: Has a new basis for making rulings been added?

Messages.Author: Mike Bohlmann
Messages.Body:
Until now, I can't recall a card ever being errata'd/ruled
on/clarified
on the basis of making sense in the game world. ie Sengir Dagger
with Torn Signpost, being able to prevent the damage from Rutor's
Hand (how do you prevent the damage from cutting out your eye and
your hand off anyway? :)

However, some of the new rulings from LSJ seem to indicate that a move
towards making cards make sense in the game world has been made.
Immortal Grapple sticks out as a prime example:

> > I fail to see why it was needed to remove this specific
> > exception. Why is this necessary?
>
> To make the card function as it originally should have (IMHO),

An aside:

So are all cards going to be changed back to Jyhad wording? I'd
love to see Archon changed back. However, I would rather not.
Even though Jyhad backed cards are available with abundancy on the
net, they aren't everywhere else. Is the general rule that newer
card text takes precedence over old card text being thrown out the
window or just in IG's case? Btw, did my long post on the IG ruling/
errata go through? I didn't see a reply from LSJ.....

> and
> to make it make sense (how can I continue to grapple you if you move
> to long range?)

Think of it as this. The other vampire isn't actually maneuvering
to long range, but is fighting against your grip well enough that
you can't get a hit in; you're spending all your energy just trying
to hold on. When you have superior potence, they have no chance of
breaking your grip. :)

This reason for errataing the card makes it appear that there is a
new basis for making rulings and errata: making sense in the game
world. So is Torn Signpost going to be changed to be a one-combat
melee weapon that sets your base hand damage? That certainly makes
sense in the game world (I'm not trying to sound facetious[sp?]).
If one ruling is made based on "making a card make sense" is that
going to open a whole can of worms that the game really needs to go
into? The Golconda and RtI rulings appear to make it seem so
(although
I think those are great errata, IMHO, I don't think they were
absolutely necessary. *)

Just so you know where I'm coming from, I'm of the opinion that
cards should only be changed on an individual basis if there is a
weird situation that can occur that makes the card work in unexpected
ways.

Mike

--

Mike Bohlmann, MAIP mboh...@pdnt.com
Internet Strategy and Development Consultant

>
> However, some of the new rulings from LSJ seem to indicate that a move
> towards making cards make sense in the game world has been made.
> Immortal Grapple sticks out as a prime example:

Good points, and a good concern.

Game-world sensibility is not being used to make errata.
Just because a card/combo/rule doesn't make sense from a
game world perspective *doesn't* mean the new RT is going
to errata it to make sense.

But, when a change (back to intended meaning, to fix problems, to
lessen confusion) is made, and it happens to make more sense
from a "game world" point of view, that's usually an indication
that the change is on the right track.

The errata on the VTES/Sabbat versions of IGrapple is made to
return the card to function as it was originally designed -
that is, to undo the previous ruling on the default duration of
combat cards' effects that got added (as errata to the Jyhad
version) in the VTES/Sabbat printings of the card.

That the change makes more sense in the game world is an
added bonus.

> Btw, did my long post on the IG ruling/
> errata go through? I didn't see a reply from LSJ.....

It's out there, somewhere.

> from the text of lasting the entire combat, then why not change
> the other card that specifies lasting the entire combat: Torn
> Signpost?
> Also, what was ambiguous or confusing about the default duration
> of combat cards in general and IG in particular
>

You're not listening. Torn Signpost says that it lasts all combat.
Therfore it does. The original version of Immortal Grapple did not say
how long it lasted. For some reason, the rules team made a ruling and
said that it would last all combat. This was contrary to the intent of
the card, but they didn't care. To reflect this ruling, new versions of
Immortal Grapple were made with reminder text that said they lasted all
combat. Just recently there was a clear ruling made that said if combat
cards don't say how long they last, then they're only good for the
round. Applying this to Immortal Grapple makes the reminder text
*wrong.* Therefore, the reminder text has been errata'd out so that the
card works according to the new ruling and as it was originally
intended.

-Chris

And yet, that still doesn't explain why it was a good change to make. I
understand that LSJ now has all the authority in the world to do what he
did, and the manner in which he did it was correct. I just don't agree
(and despite what you may believe _many_ other people share this
sentiment) that this was a good change to make.

I would like some sort of reason other than "this is the way it was
originally intented" which can never be anything other than opinion, and
"it makes sense in the game world" which has never before been a reason
for changing anything.

> > It doesn't *look* like reminder text on the card. As someone pointed out
> > in a previous post, reminder text is generally in parenthesis.
>

> Not always. Many (D) bleed cards in Sabbat say "(D) Bleed any
> methuselah..." That's not in parentheses, but it is still reminder
> text. If some ruling were to be made that said (D) bleeds could only be
> made against your prey, this reminder text would be incorrect and would
> need to be errata'd out.

But if the ruling were to say "(D) bleeds can only be made against your
prey except where the card says otherwise", these card would not be
eratta'd unless there was some other reason.

The new rule _should_ apply to Blood of Acid, which doesn't say that it
lasts the entire combat. But Immortal Grapple, which was printed in the
same set, _does_ say that it lasts the entire combat. It seems to me
that at the time these cards were printed, Immortal Grapple was intended
to last the entire combat. But LSJ doesn't like that so he changed it.
Fine.

> Distraction(inf) says "Replace this card, then
> draw 5 cards and discard down to your maximum hand size." All it needs
> to say is "Draw 5 cards." You replace the card as soon as it leaves
> your hand (well before the action resolves and the card tells you to
> replace). And after drawing, you must always go back to your maximum
> hand size unless it says that it increases your hand size (like Dreams
> of the Sphinx). Therefore, everything besides "draw 5 cards" is
> reminder text. Do you see parentheses?

No, that text is not reminder text. If the card said just "draw 5
cards", you would have to draw the cards one at a time, discarding after
you drew each one. "Draw 5 cards and discard to your maximum hand size"
is a different effect, and the extra text is needed in that case.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
>
> No, that text is not reminder text. If the card said just "draw 5
> cards", you would have to draw the cards one at a time, discarding after
> you drew each one. "Draw 5 cards and discard to your maximum hand size"
> is a different effect, and the extra text is needed in that case.
>

Actually, if it said "Draw 5 cards," you would draw all 5 at once. It
wouldn't say to pause in between them. It's all one instruction and
actually, to follow the letter of the law, you'd have to take all 5 off
of your deck at one time and put them in your hand. No looking at cards
between drawing card 2 and card 3. If it said "Draw a card. Draw
another card. Draw a third card. Now draw another card. Finally draw
one more card." Then, I assume that you'd have to discard between draws
(but there'd be some confusion about that). So, discarding is indeed
reminder text.

(Not sure why I'm arguing this, as the point here only applies in a
peripheral way to the argument at hand, and the wording of this mythical
card doesn't really matter. Oh well, maybe I just like arguing...) 8)

-Chris
